transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-10-03 15:00 UTC | Duration: 49m | Recording: yes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Marco Lee (Redwood CSM), Ben O'Neal (Sunward Head of Platform), Leila Haddad (CTO), Ravi Patel (Infra)
Shared: renewal deck (drive link), eu-edge runbook (internal link)

Auto-summary (auto): Quick renewal check-in, discuss EU edge provisioning timeline, clarify capacity uplift for Q4, confirm compliance artifacts and next steps.

Topics: renewal terms, dedicated vs hosted capacity, EU region list, VPC/on-prem constraints, KMS & audit logs, latency SLOs, provisioning timeline, benchmark plan.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. quick check in before the quarter close. Ben, you had sent over the usage snapshot, is that still the latest?
[00:18] Ben O'Neal: Yeah, that's the one, the - uh - the Q3 burst was bigger than expected, we hit around 2.6k rps for a short window. the deck has the breakdown. sorry, my network's a bit noisy.
[00:30] Priya Desai: I can see the sheet, thanks. So high level today: renewal cadence, confirm if you're going with dedicated capacity or staying hosted with burst, and walk through the EU edge onprem / vpc plan.
[00:45] Leila Haddad: We're leaning toward dedicated for predictable latency, but we need clarity on the provisioning lead time, because compliance wants EU-located instances and our KMS integration must be in place.
[01:05] Alex Chen: Totally, that aligns with other customers. To scope pricing we'll show two commitment tiers — baseline and burst capacity. I'll follow up with exact numbers.
[01:18] Ravi Patel: One technical note — our infra team uses a private peering model, we can't do public egress for tokens. so any VPC wiring steps, please highlight.
[01:33] Priya Desai: Good point. The EU edge runbook (I'll share after) includes VPC peering patterns and sample terraform. keep in mind some of the wording in the runbook is auto-gen so there might be typos like "KV cash" instead of KV cache, sorry about that.
[01:55] Marco Lee: Also, Ben asked earlier about SLA tiers and fallbacks. if dedicated goes down we have automatic fallback to compatible hosted variants — we can show the failover policy.
[02:10] Ben O'Neal: That's useful. what's the typical failover latency spike? We need numbers for the ops playbook.
[02:22] Priya Desai: In our experience, spike to ~2x latency for about 20–90 seconds depending on cache warmup. we'll add a baseline latency spreadsheet but obviously depends on model + seq length.
[02:44] Leila Haddad: Can you share an example latency for a 2k token LLM call? our average seq length is around 512 tokens though.
[02:56] Priya Desai: For 512 tokens on A100-style infra at EU edge, typical tail p95 is in the 300–450ms range with continuous batching disabled; with batching and cache warm prefixes you can drop unit cost by 20–35%. these are approximate.
[03:22] Ravi Patel: Which model flavors are you recommending? quantized or fp16? our legal team worries about accuracy regressions with heavy quant.
[03:35] Alex Chen: We usually recommend q4_0 or q8_0 for production, but we run evals against your prompt sets to verify. Redwood Optimize gives recommendations per workload.
[03:50] Ben O'Neal: who from Redwood will run the evals?
[03:55] Priya Desai: I'll coordinate with our applied ML team; we can run a 2-week pilot eval in staging. need your eval prompt set and some sample traffic.
[04:10] Leila Haddad: Timeline question — if we sign a 12-month renewal by mid-Oct, what is realistic for EU edge activation?
[04:20] Alex Chen: If we have signed commitment and region list, provisioning usually takes 3–4 weeks for EU edge (including peering and KMS). on-prem options add more time. so signing mid-Oct -> activation early to mid-Nov is feasible.
[04:45] Ben O'Neal: ok that fits our Q4 go-live target. can you put that in writing?
[04:50] Alex Chen: yes, I'll add it to the quote and include an activation timeline.
[05:05] Ravi Patel: about KMS — we need compatibility with our HSM provider, and the kms key policies must allow cross-account decrypt for your control plane. we also need audit logs retained for 12 months.
[05:22] Marco Lee: we'll share our KMS integration note. SOC2 report and audit log retention are standard for enterprise — I'll open a support ticket with the artifacts.
[05:35] Ben O'Neal: any blockers around data residency? we've got legal asking for EU-only processing for PII.
[05:45] Priya Desai: With dedicated EU edge we can guarantee compute and KV cache in-region. control plane metadata may still traverse region X unless you choose private (Redwood Privet?) — sorry i mean Redwood Private — where control plane is customer-managed in a VPC. we'll clarify in the doc.
[06:12] Leila Haddad: can you confirm whether metadata passes through US or stays in EU for the Private option?
[06:20] Alex Chen: For Redwood Private deployed in your VPC the control plane is in-region so metadata stays in-region. for Hosted with EU edge, control plane endpoints are region-aware but some telemetry may pass through our central telemetry cluster unless configured otherwise. we'll get the exact wording.
[06:44] Ben O'Neal: competitors — another vendor (MegaCloud AI) promised a 2-week activation but their pricing was opaque; any risks with Redwood's 3–4 week estimate?
[06:57] Priya Desai: The 3–4 weeks factors in network approvals, peering, and KMS ops. if your network team pre-approves CIDR ranges and we get the creds early we can compress to ~10 business days.
[07:18] Ravi Patel: talk to our network team first. we'll send the firewall & peering template.
[07:26] Ben O'Neal: okay. on pricing: for committed dedicated capacity do you offer refunds or true-up?
[07:35] Alex Chen: We have monthly true-up options and burst credits; refunds aren't standard but we can discuss flexible commit tiers — e.g., baseline commitment + buffer burst pool billed at a lower rate than pure on-demand.
[07:50] Leila Haddad: can you send a 12-month example with three tiers? baseline, mid, and enterprise burst?
[07:58] Alex Chen: Yes — I'll send two proposals: 12-month and 24-month with pricing and the associated SLOs.
[08:08] Priya Desai: back to tech — Ravi, a couple of gotchas: public egress for model hotswaps, and if you enable KV cache prefetch across regions you'll need additional egress allowances. also note the runbook has a couple of typos; it's been through a raw pass.
[08:29] Ravi Patel: noted. we'll want a readout with the exact egress estimates per region to feed procurement.
[08:38] Marco Lee: i'll coordinate with billing to include egress estimates and expected monthly invoice impact for the tiers.
[08:46] Ben O'Neal: any legal redlines we should anticipate for a 12-month extension?
[08:52] Alex Chen: standard clauses: data residency, liability caps, and SLA credits. our legal team can pre-share the redlines doc.
[09:00] Leila Haddad: great. can we also get the SOC2 type II report?
[09:05] Marco Lee: yes, opening ticket now.
[09:09] Alex Chen: ok we have action items: I'll send pricing, Priya shares runbook and benchmark template, Marco to open support ticket for SOC2/KMS notes, Ben to confirm regions. agreed due dates?
[09:20] Ben O'Neal: target all by next week if possible.
[09:24] Alex Chen: we'll aim for that. Any final technical questions?
[09:30] Ravi Patel: one more — how do canary rollouts work if we push a model variant across EU edge? downtime risk?
[09:39] Priya Desai: Canary is per-route; we do shadow traffic then 5–10% rollout. KV cache warming is the main risk but we have pre-warm hooks. downtime is rare.
[09:53] Leila Haddad: ok thanks.

[10:10] (Later in call, scheduling/planning)
[10:10] Alex Chen: Recap — action items and next steps. we'll share the renewal quote + activation timeline + runbook + SOC2. schedule provisioning workshop week of Oct 11.
[10:25] Ben O'Neal: sounds good, thanks all.

End of transcript.
